time.method: Distances are measured along real roads and footpaths from the house. Car (GrabCar): road distance at an average of 18 km/h – a realistic Saigon daytime speed including traffic – plus 3 min for pickup and parking; for trips over 20 km (mostly highway) a faster highway estimate is used. Motorbike (GrabBike): the shorter of the car route and the motorbike route (small streets and bridges) at 22 km/h, plus 2 min. Walk: footpath route at 4.5 km/h. Times are rounded to 5 minutes (minimum 5). Where a car route was more than twice as long as the walking route without crossing the canal (a U-turn on a divided road), car and motorbike use the walking distance + 15 %. Rush hour (approx. 7–9 am and 4:30–7 pm) and rain can make trips longer; late at night they are often shorter.

attractions.title: Things to do
attractions.sub: Sights, markets, parks, nightlife and a day trip · Ho Chi Minh City
attractions.intro: Welcome! Your 3-bedroom riverside home sits in Tân Hưng (former District 7), next to District 4 and about 20 minutes by car from the city centre. Head up to the rooftop for river and skyline views, then use this guide to plan your days. Each place on the map shows its distance and time by car, motorbike and on foot; details are in the table on the next page.
tips: Getting around

Use the Grab app (or Be / Xanh SM) for cars and motorbike taxis: fixed fares, no haggling, pay by card or cash. Show drivers the Vietnamese name in this guide. Our address for the ride home: 389A Trần Xuân Soạn, Tân Hưng.
Traffic

Rush hours are roughly 7–9 am and 4:30–7 pm; travel times can double. Times in this guide assume normal daytime traffic (car about 18 km/h, motorbike about 22 km/h); late at night trips are often quicker.
Best time to visit
Dry season is Dec–Apr. In the rainy season (May–Nov) expect short, heavy afternoon showers: plan museums for the afternoon and carry a light poncho.
Temples & pagodas
Cover shoulders and knees, remove shoes where asked, speak quietly, and ask before photographing people praying.
Opening hours
Museums in HCMC do not generally close for lunch. Check individual opening hours; e.g. Dinh Độc Lập is open daily 07:00–18:00. Night markets and food streets get going after 5 pm.
Money & safety
Currency is the Vietnamese đồng (VND); ATMs are everywhere. Keep phones away from the curb side (bag snatching happens), and cross streets slowly and steadily.
Heat & health
Drink bottled water, use sunscreen, and plan outdoor sights for early morning. Ice in restaurants is generally made from purified water.
Emergencies
Police 113 · Fire 114 · Ambulance 115. International clinics include FV Hospital (District 7 area) and Family Medical Practice.

shopping.title: Shopping
shopping.sub: Quận 4 & Quận 7 · Malls, markets, supermarkets, convenience stores
shopping.intro: All the important shopping options in Quận 4 and Quận 7: the big malls, local markets, supermarkets, convenience stores, pharmacies and ATMs, each with distance and time by car, motorbike and on foot.
tips: Cash at markets
At the chợ (markets) almost everything is paid in cash (VND, small notes). Malls, supermarkets and convenience stores usually take cards.
Go early
Local markets are freshest in the morning; many stalls close in the afternoon. Big chains and malls are open all day.
Prices & haggling
Food prices at markets are usually low; haggling is normal for clothes and souvenirs at market stalls, but not in malls or supermarkets.
Grab to the malls
For the malls, Grab (car or motorbike) is easiest: cheap and no parking hassle. For the ride home, just show our address: 389A Trần Xuân Soạn, Tân Hưng.
Mind the Kênh Tẻ
The house is right on the south bank of the Kênh Tẻ canal. Places on the north side (Quận 4:) look close but can only be reached via bridges:– km by car, approx. 2–2.8 km by motorbike or on foot.
Walking
Up to about 1.5 km (e.g. and all pharmacies & ATMs) walking is pleasant. For longer trips Grab is the better choice in heat or rain; pavements are often blocked by parked motorbikes.
Bách Hóa Xanh

The big Vietnamese grocery chain (usually 06:30–21:30) is listed above with three branches. According to the chain's branch lists there are more nearby: 2–2A Đường số 17, 181 Lê Văn Lương, 343 Lê Văn Lương and 412–412A Lê Văn Lương – just search “Bách Hóa Xanh” in Google Maps. Fresh food is often discounted in the evening.
Pharmacies & ATMs
Pharmacies and ATMs are all within walking distance. Big malls also have ATMs and money exchange. Emergency ambulance: dial 115 – for anything serious go to a hospital rather than a pharmacy.
Drinking water & bags
Don't drink tap water; bottled water is sold in every convenience store. Bring your own shopping bag.

relaxation.title: Relaxation
relaxation.sub: Quận 4 & Quận 7 · Spas, massage, parks, swimming pools
relaxation.intro: Day spas, massage, parks and swimming pools in Quận 4 and Quận 7, each with distance and time by car, motorbike and on foot. ★ = top recommendation.
tips: Tipping
Tipping your massage therapist is customary in Vietnamese spas and appreciated; the amount is up to you. Some spas include it in the price – just ask at reception.
Call ahead
Good spas are busy in the evening and at weekends. A quick call saves waiting time; Google Translate helps at small places.
Confirm prices
Have price and duration confirmed before the treatment; promotional prices often apply only at certain times.
Golden Lotus (jjimjilbang)
Plan 2–4 hours. Entry is cheapest in the evening and on weekday mornings; current promotions are on the official website.
Hồ Bán Nguyệt in the evening
The light show on the Cầu Ánh Sao (Starlight Bridge) runs Thu–Sun evenings. Bring mosquito repellent; park at Crescent Mall.
Kênh Tẻ
The house is right on the south bank of the canal. Places in Quận 4 are often closer on foot or by motorbike than by car. A new riverside promenade along the canal is expected by 2028.
Heat & rain
Walks are best early in the morning or after 5 pm; in the rainy season (approx. May–November) there are often short, heavy afternoon showers. For distances over approx. 2 km, take a Grab.
Gyms
For gyms in Quận 7 we found no official day-pass prices, only monthly memberships – ask directly if you're interested.

spa: For half a day of relaxation – also ideal when it rains.
massage: Well-rated massage spas in Quận 7 and Quận 4. Confirm price and duration before the treatment.
park: Best early in the morning (approx. 6–8 am) or after 5 pm.

restaurants.title: Japanese, Korean & Chinese food
restaurants.intro: Selected, well-rated restaurants – only in Quận 4 and Quận 7 – from cheap snack bars to upscale dinners. ★ = our top tips.
tips: Book ahead
Korean BBQ in Phú Mỹ Hưng, Haidilao and Dim Tu Tac are full on Friday and Saturday evenings – call shortly before or book or the restaurant's Facebook page.
Banchan
In Korean restaurants the small side dishes are free and usually refilled. Often the rule is: at least one main dish per person.
Let them grill
At Korean BBQ the staff usually grill for you – just ask.
Dim sum
Dim sum is best at lunchtime (yum cha); some restaurants close between lunch and dinner.
Vegetarian/vegan
TOJY is a fully plant-based Japanese restaurant and the closest restaurant on the list.
Paying
Larger restaurants and the malls take cards; small places often only cash or QR bank transfer. Some bills add 8–10% VAT.
Crescent Mall cluster
Sachi, C.Tao, Haidilao, Shang Garden and Yeebo are close together – easy to combine with shopping or an evening walk around Crescent Lake (Hồ Bán Nguyệt).
Kênh Tẻ canal
The house is right on the south bank of the canal. Restaurants in Quận 4 are often much closer on foot or by motorbike than by car, because cars have to detour via the bridges.

jp: From vegetarian sushi around the corner and small ramen shops to upscale sushi in Crescent Mall.
kr: Phú Mỹ Hưng is Saigon's “Koreatown”: Korean BBQ with lots of free side dishes (banchan, usually refilled), stews and noodles. Cheap Korean snack bars also in Quận 4.
cn: Dim sum, Cantonese roast goose, hotpot and Taiwanese noodles – around Crescent Mall, in Him Lam and in Quận 4.

drinks.title: Evening drinks
drinks.sub: Quận 4 & Quận 7 · beer restaurants, bars, craft beer, rooftops, two new areas & Vĩnh Khánh food street
drinks.intro: Hand-picked, well-reviewed places in Quận 4 and Quận 7 only. ★ = top tips · 🍺 = alcohol confirmed · ❓ = alcohol unknown.
tips: How to order nhậu style
Beer comes by the glass, jug or bucket of cans with ice; food is ordered a few plates at a time and shared. Staff keep a running tab – you pay at the end.
Vĩnh Khánh street
Busiest from about 18:00 to midnight. Point at dishes on neighbouring tables or ask for an English menu (Ốc Đào 2 has one). Agree on the price of seafood sold by weight before it is cooked.
Getting home

Grab (bike or car) is cheap and easy: the Vĩnh Khánh and Bến Vân Đồn places are about min by car or min by motorbike, Phú Mỹ Hưng about min by car. Show the driver our address: 389A Trần Xuân Soạn, Tân Hưng.
Don't drink and ride
Vietnam has a zero-alcohol limit for drivers and riders. Never ride a motorbike after drinking – take a GrabCar or GrabBike instead.
Paying
Bars and taprooms usually take cards; small quán nhậu often only cash or QR bank transfer.
Night Town & Crescent Lake
Sky Garden Night Town is liveliest after 18:00; combine it with a walk around Phú Mỹ Hưng or Crescent Lake (Hồ Bán Nguyệt), where WBW and the Pasteur Street Phú Mỹ Hưng taproom are.

nhau: Nhậu is how Saigon unwinds: plastic stools on the pavement, buckets of ice, cheap beer and plates of food to share. Bia hơi is fresh, light draught beer in the Hanoi style, served by the glass or jug. Quận 4's Vĩnh Khánh food street (a designated food street since 2018 and one of Time Out's ‘Coolest Streets in the World’ in 2025) is the classic place for snails, seafood and beer; it is only about 1.2 km away as the crow flies, but because of the canal it is about min on foot or min by car.
bar: From a live-music bar and a rooftop with skyline views (both close to the house) to the craft-beer taprooms of Phú Mỹ Hưng.
new: The Sky Garden food & commerce street in Phú Mỹ Hưng (opened 30 August 2024) runs as a night street from 18:00 to 24:00, between Nguyễn Văn Linh, Phạm Văn Nghị, Đường số 2 and Bùi Bằng Đoàn.

Busy with after-work groups, families and birthday parties; football is shown on big screens. The closest proper beer restaurant to the homestay.

drink-quan-an-khanh-q7-bia-hoi-ha-noi.name: Quán An Khánh Q7 – Bia Hơi Hà Nội
drink-quan-an-khanh-q7-bia-hoi-ha-noi.note: Small, very well-rated neighbourhood bia hơi with Hanoi home cooking – reviewers single out the crispy fried rice and the fish dishes, and the fragrant, cold draught beer. Walking distance from the homestay. Street 11N (Cư xá Ngân Hàng) is earmarked by the district as a future weekend food/walking street, but its opening has not been confirmed.

drink-lo-thien-quan.note: Lively, very local open-air drinking restaurant ('lộ thiên' means open-air) tucked away in a residential street: outdoor seating, a wide choice of dishes, cold beer and a cheerful, noisy atmosphere; the staff even put on short birthday shows. No English menu, according to reviewers.

drink-brightside-bar.note: Live-music bar close to the homestay with live bands, open-mic and DJ nights, a creative cocktail menu, imported beers and bar snacks.

drink-bia-tuoi-kho-muc.note: Small, simple draught-beer spot – 'bia tươi' is fresh draught beer and 'khô mực' (dried squid) is the classic beer snack. Tucked into the lane at 178/4a Nguyễn Hữu Thọ on the south-east side of the junction. Very new, with only one Google review so far.

drink-than-hoa-quan.note: Small charcoal-grill eatery ('than hoả' means charcoal fire) at 178 Nguyễn Hữu Thọ, on the south-east side of the junction. New, with only four Google reviews so far.

drink-joyjoy-garden.note: Open-air beer garden on the newly opened food lot at 40 Ngô Thị Bì – the north-east corner of the big Nguyễn Hữu Thọ × Ngô Thị Bì junction, opposite Sunrise City View. Opening hours are not yet, so check before you go; evenings are the time to come.

drink-quan-bia-set.name: Quán Bia Sệt (listed as “Quan Bia Set”)
drink-quan-bia-set.note: Big, busy beer restaurant at the start of Nguyễn Hữu Thọ known for 'bia sệt' – beer served ice-cold until it turns slushy – plus a long list of drinking snacks. Good for groups.

drink-aroma-hops-eatery-drinks.note: Small, cosy bar-eatery with friendly English-speaking bartenders, classic cocktails, beer and bottle service, good music and tasty, affordable drinking food. Few reviews so far, but all very positive.

drink-bia-hoi-ha-noi-hoan-luong.note: Very highly rated Hanoi bia hơi with outdoor seating: beer poured fresh from the tap, northern dishes including goat meat, cheerful noisy atmosphere – reviewers say it is perfect for big groups of 20+.

drink-thuong-rooftop.note: Rooftop café-bar on the 7th floor with retro décor and a wide view over the city towards Landmark 81 and Bitexco – great for sunset. Cocktails, mocktails, beer and snacks at modest prices. Opens in the late afternoon and gets busy with couples and groups after dark.
drink-thuong-rooftop.price: drinks approx. 35,000–99,000 VND (1 Phút Sài Gòn)

drink-toi-ben-food-beer.note: Large, no-frills quán nhậu on Bến Vân Đồn with fresh seafood and classic drinking dishes, popular with office groups and football fans late into the night.

drink-quan-oc-kenh-te-2.note: Local snail-and-seafood (ốc) eatery on the District 4 side of the Kênh Tẻ canal, a little hard to find. Reviewers praise big, fresh snails and seafood at fair prices (the salted-egg-sauce snails are a favourite), with an English-speaking waiter; it gets crowded at weekends and dishes can take a while. Just across the canal, so it is quick to reach.

drink-nha-hang-wbw-world-of-beers-wine.name: Nhà Hàng WBW – World of Beers & Wine
drink-nha-hang-wbw-world-of-beers-wine.note: Beer-and-wine restaurant at the Hồ Bán Nguyệt (Crescent Lake): a large selection of local and international beers on tap and in bottles (including Belgian), live music and football on weekends.

drink-oc-oanh.note: The most famous – and most crowded – snail restaurant on Vĩnh Khánh street, with thousands of reviews. Big menu of snails, clams, prawns, octopus and grilled chicken feet; beer by the can or bottle. Expect queues and a tourist crowd at peak times; the rating is mixed, but the atmosphere is the real Vĩnh Khánh experience.

drink-mr-craft-craft-beer-wine.name: Mr Craft – Craft Beer & Wine
drink-mr-craft-craft-beer-wine.note: Craft beer and wine bar with around 20 taps, just east of the Night Town zone. Reviewers like the IPAs, tacos, oysters and chicken wings, sports on TV and live bands on Saturday nights.

drink-the-gioi-bo-nuong-sot-va-lau.name: Thế Giới Bò – Nướng, Sốt và Lẩu
drink-the-gioi-bo-nuong-sot-va-lau.note: 'Beef World' at the northern end of Vĩnh Khánh: beef grilled at the table, beef in sauces and beef hotpot. Outdoor tables are cooler and less smoky; little English is spoken. Beer is Tiger or Heineken.

drink-bia-hoi-ha-noi-80a-bia-hoi-80a-qua.name: Bia Hơi Hà Nội 80A (Quận 4)
drink-bia-hoi-ha-noi-80a-bia-hoi-80a-qua.note: Authentic Hanoi bia hơi on the Bến Vân Đồn riverside road: little plastic chairs, light fresh draught beer by the jug, garlic snails, tamarind clams and peanuts, full of locals and few tourists. Tip from a reviewer: there is a second bia hơi next door – 80A is the one with the blue chairs, not the corner one.

drink-oc-dao-2.note: One of the best-known snail restaurants on Vĩnh Khánh food street. Has an English menu that lists the cooking styles (grilled, garlic butter, tamarind, etc.), which makes ordering easy. Cheap beer, eaten street-side among locals.

drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-phu-my-h.name: Pasteur Street Craft Beer – Phú Mỹ Hưng Taproom & Restaurant
drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-phu-my-h.note: Pasteur Street's taproom and restaurant in the Crescent Residence complex near Crescent Mall and the Hồ Bán Nguyệt lake – craft beer on tap with a full menu; easy to combine with an evening walk around the lake.

drink-el-baron-saigon-whiskey-cigar-loun.name: El Barón Saigon – Whiskey & Cigar Lounge
drink-el-baron-saigon-whiskey-cigar-loun.note: Refined whiskey and cigar lounge for quiet conversations, date nights and small celebrations, with reserved seating and attentive service. The upmarket option in the Night Town zone.

drink-ruby-soho.note: Rock 'n' roll pub inside the Night Town zone, decorated with music and film memorabilia, with a street-side patio for watching the evening bustle. Good cocktails, fairly priced beer, private rooms upstairs and a mix of locals and expats; live music nights.

drink-tiem-bia-ga-rooster-beers-taproom-.note: Casual, retro-style taproom of the local Rooster Beers brewery – affordable craft beer, a laid-back crowd and only a few simple snacks. The farthest bar on this map.

drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-nguyen-d.name: Pasteur Street Craft Beer – Nguyễn Đức Cảnh Taproom
drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-nguyen-d.note: NEW: Vietnam's pioneering craft brewery opened this taproom (its 14th) on 5 September 2025. Rotating Pasteur Street craft beers on tap plus a full food menu.

drink-moon-1984-rooftop.note: Korean-style rooftop bar in the heart of the Night Town zone: cocktails, beer and soju happy hours, Korean food (the kimchi pancake gets praise) and fun party games. Good for dates and groups.

drink-the-tavern-pmh.note: Long-running sports bar and pub (around 20 years) with Western and Mexican pub food, live sports on big screens (Premier League, F1, UFC, AFL), a free pool table, regular live music and quiz nights. Happy hour Mon–Fri 16:00–19:00. On the eastern edge of the Night Town zone.

fam-ho-boi-sky-garden.note: Public day-ticket pool with a children's area. Phone +84 28 5410 3008.

relax-cong-vien-nam-vien.note: Quiet landscaped park made of three connected parks (over 630 m long, approx. 45,000 m²) with lakes, pavilions and about 10,000 m² of footpaths – popular for jogging, yoga and picnics. Free entry.

relax-ho-ban-nguyet-crescent-lake-cau-an.note: The nicest evening walk in District 7: promenade around the crescent-shaped lake, the 170 m illuminated “Starlight Bridge”, approx. 20 ha of park, right next to Crescent Mall. Free entry.

fam-khu-choi-xe-dien-tre-em-ho-ban-nguye.note: Evening ride-on toy cars by the Crescent Lake (Hồ Bán Nguyệt) and Starlight Bridge. Best after sunset.

fam-tastemaker-hub-lop-nau-an-cooking-cl.note: Bookable personalised cooking classes for families/groups – not a dedicated kids' class; ask about ages. Phone 070 595 8488.
fam-tastemaker-hub-lop-nau-an-cooking-cl.price: personalised classes for families from 500,000 VND

relax-cong-vien-kenh-dao-phu-my-hung.note: Green paths along the man-made canal network of Phú Mỹ Hưng – good for walking and jogging, only a few minutes from Hồ Bán Nguyệt.

fam-waterway-premium-kids-club-cafe.note: Covered kids' pool plus dry play – the best rainy/hot-day pool option. Phone 077 889 9320.
fam-waterway-premium-kids-club-cafe.price: weekday play 99k / pool 149k / combo 199k; weekend 149k / 199k / 249k; 2nd parent +49k; under 1: 50%

fam-yoyo-kidsplay-cafe.note: Kids café with play area in the south of the old District 7; hours/prices unconfirmed.

attr-thao-cam-vien.name: Saigon Zoo & Botanical Gardens
attr-thao-cam-vien.note: One of the world's oldest zoos (1864): shady gardens, elephants, giraffes, playgrounds. Go early morning.

attr-cong-vien-van-hoa-dam-sen.name: Đầm Sen Park
attr-cong-vien-van-hoa-dam-sen.note: Large amusement and cultural park with rides, lakes and gardens; the Đầm Sen water park is next door.

attr-ben-bach-dang.name: Bạch Đằng Wharf & River Cruises
attr-ben-bach-dang.note: Riverside park and pier for Saigon Waterbus rides and dinner cruises; lovely skyline at night.

attr-thap-bitexco.name: Saigon Skydeck (Bitexco Tower)
attr-thap-bitexco.note: 49th-floor observation deck in the lotus-shaped tower; 360° views over the river. Sunset is best.

attr-pho-di-bo-nguyen-hue.name: Nguyễn Huệ Walking Street
attr-pho-di-bo-nguyen-hue.note: Pedestrian boulevard with fountains, City Hall and the Opera House nearby; lively and family-friendly in the evening.

attr-nha-tho-duc-ba.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral Basilica
attr-nha-tho-duc-ba.note: Red-brick 1880 French cathedral, the city's icon (exterior under restoration at times). Great photo stop.

attr-dinh-doc-lap.name: Independence Palace
attr-dinh-doc-lap.note: 1960s palace where the Vietnam War ended in 1975; war rooms, bunker and tanks on the lawn. Easy walk-through for all ages.

attr-bao-tang-chung-tich-chien-tranh.name: War Remnants Museum
attr-bao-tang-chung-tich-chien-tranh.note: Powerful museum on the Vietnam War with aircraft and tanks outside. Some galleries are graphic; preview before bringing young children.

attr-buu-dien-trung-tam-sai-gon.name: Saigon Central Post Office
attr-buu-dien-trung-tam-sai-gon.note: Elegant 1891 post office opposite the cathedral; send a postcard home. Book Street (Đường Sách) is next door.

attr-hoi-quan-tue-thanh.name: Thiên Hậu Temple (Chợ Lớn)
attr-hoi-quan-tue-thanh.note: Ornate 18th-century Chinese temple to the sea goddess, with giant hanging incense coils.

attr-chua-ngoc-hoang.name: Jade Emperor Pagoda
attr-chua-ngoc-hoang.note: Atmospheric 1909 Taoist pagoda full of incense and carved deities; turtle pond kids love.

attr-landmark-81.name: Landmark 81 SkyView
attr-landmark-81.note: Vietnam's tallest tower: SkyView deck (floors 79-81), Vincom mall and riverside park below.

attr-thao-dien.name: Thảo Điền (Thủ Đức)
attr-thao-dien.note: Leafy expat neighbourhood with cafés, brunch spots, boutiques and riverside bars; relaxed for families.

shop-cho-tan-kieng-1.note: The closest market to the homestay – a small, everyday neighbourhood market on Trần Xuân Soạn, about 550 m west of the homestay. Perfect for a first look at a Vietnamese wet market and a cheap breakfast.
shop-cho-tan-kieng-1.hours: 6:00 am – 6:30 pm daily; OpenStreetMap lists 5:00 am – 9:00 pm

shop-circle-k-lam-van-ben.note: Open around the clock: drinks, snacks, ready meals.

shop-gs25.note: Korean convenience store with snacks and hot food.

shop-cho-cu-xa-ngan-hang.note: Small neighbourhood market for daily needs in the Cư xá Ngân Hàng residential area.

shop-bach-hoa-xanh.note: Bách Hóa Xanh branch on the same street as the house (to the west). According to reviews, meat is discounted from 6–7 pm, but then it gets busy.

shop-cho-tan-quy.note: Locals call it the 'morning market'. The covered hall itself is quiet these days – the real market happens outside: a long line of vendors' carts and pavement stalls fills Đường số 17 and the side streets around the hall. One of the liveliest street markets near the homestay.
shop-cho-tan-quy.hours: Main market early morning until about noon; a smaller afternoon session from about 3:30 pm to 6 pm

mkt-cho-chieu-tan-quy.note: The 'afternoon market' of Tân Quy, where locals shop for dinner after work. Small and very local; the two bus stops on Đường số 17 are even named 'Chợ Chiều'.

shop-cho-tan-kieng-2.note: A genuinely hidden market: the small hall sits inside the block behind Lê Văn Lương, and reviewers say it is hard to find the way in if you are not local. Motorbikes can ride right in between the stalls.

shop-bach-hoa-xanh-122-lam-van-ben.note: Branch of the big Vietnamese grocery chain: fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, drinks, household goods – low fixed prices. Fresh food often discounted in the evening.

mkt-cho-tan-thuan.note: Old neighbourhood market near the Tân Thuận bridge, reached through a lane off Huỳnh Tấn Phát. Reviewers love the long-running breakfast stalls inside.

shop-satra-foods.note: Small grocery supermarket (state-owned Satra chain), fresh meat & vegetables.

shop-lotte-mart-nam-sai-gon.note: Cinema in the LOTTE Mart building (same building as kidzooona).

shop-cho-tan-my.note: Big, busy and well-stocked – the best 'real' market experience in Phú Mỹ Hưng's neighbourhood.
shop-cho-tan-my.hours: 6:00 am – 7:00 pm daily; Vietnam Mới (2021) gives 4:00 am – 6:00 pm

mkt-cho-bui-van-ba.note: A lively unofficial street market (chợ tự phát): pavement stalls line both sides of Bùi Văn Ba from Huỳnh Tấn Phát to alley 192. Factory workers from the Tân Thuận export zone shop here after their shift. Authorities have tried to clear the pavements, so the size changes over time.
mkt-cho-bui-van-ba.hours: About 7:00 am – after 8:00 pm (Thanh Niên report, 2023); busiest early morning and after factory shifts end

shop-go-nguyen-thi-thap.name: GO! Nguyễn Thị Thập (formerly Big C)
shop-go-nguyen-thi-thap.note: Large hypermarket (Central Retail) with a small shopping centre: groceries, household, electronics – good prices.

shop-bach-hoa-xanh-62f-nguyen-thi-thap.note: Bách-Hóa-Xanh-Filiale nahe GO! Nguyễn Thị Thập – praktisch zu kombinieren.

shop-vincom-nam-long.note: Small mall playground; price not confirmed (reports of 25–30k; Vincom says prices vary by site).

shop-co-op-food.note: Small Saigon Co.op grocery store for quick shopping.

mkt-cho-ly-phuc-man.note: Open-air street market without a hall: stalls sit right on Lý Phục Man street, so shoppers just pull over and buy.

mkt-cho-hang-phan-cho-nguyen-huu-hao.note: A photogenic hidden gem: the open-air market sits in the courtyard of an old U-shaped apartment block (Cư xá Vĩnh Hội), shaded by big umbrellas. The view down from the apartment block is a favourite photo motif.

mkt-cho-cau-cong-cho-doan-van-bo.note: A market with no building: shops and stalls simply line both sides of narrow Đoàn Văn Bơ street. Its traditional name is 'Chợ Cầu Cống'; on Google Maps it appears as 'Chợ Đoàn Văn Bơ'.
mkt-cho-cau-cong-cho-doan-van-bo.hours: Open all day; busiest in the morning and when workers come home in the late afternoon

shop-crescent-mall.name: Highlands Coffee Crescent Mall
shop-crescent-mall.note: Ground floor of Crescent Mall. Vietnam’s biggest café chain: phin coffee, Phindi, Freeze, tea, bánh mì.

shop-satra-foods-107-nguyen-tat-thanh.note: Small grocery supermarket in old District 4.

mkt-cho-200-xom-chieu.note: The famous 'Chợ 200' runs through alley 200 off Xóm Chiếu street, starting at the Xóm Chiếu church and ending at Tôn Đản – about 300 m of stalls on both sides. A morning wet market turns into a buzzing street-food alley in the afternoon. Less than 500 m from the homestay in a straight line, but across the Kênh Tẻ canal – see the walking and driving times.
mkt-cho-200-xom-chieu.hours: Wet market from about 5 am until about 11 am; street-food stalls from about 2–4 pm until about 11 pm

shop-cho-xom-chieu.note: District 4's only official traditional market, built in 1985. Shop for fresh food in the morning; in the late afternoon and evening the streets around the hall turn into a food paradise – snails (ốc), phá lấu, crab soup and chè.
shop-cho-xom-chieu.hours: Market 4:00 am – 7:00 pm; food stalls around the hall roughly 4:00 – 11:00 pm

shop-sc-vivocity.note: Free rooftop playground with water-play area, renewed in 2025 ("Ocean Park" theme). Bring swimwear and a towel for the water area.

shop-winmart-place.note: Full-range supermarket of the WinMart chain.

shop-sieu-thi-finelife-urban-hill.note: Premium supermarket with imported goods – good for Western products.

mkt-cho-kho-11.note: Tiny market at the eastern tip of District 4 – listed by the city's Department of Industry and Trade (address there: Nguyễn Thần Hiến). Very local, rarely visited by tourists.

mkt-cho-phu-thuan.note: Small 'village-style' neighbourhood market at the end of a lane off Gò Ô Môi. As reviewers put it, the hall at the end of the road is quiet while the market spilling outside along the access road is busy.

attr-cho-ho-thi-ky.name: Hồ Thị Kỷ Market & Food Alley

attr-cho-ben-thanh.name: Bến Thành Market

attr-cho-binh-tay.name: Bình Tây Market (Chợ Lớn)
attr-cho-binh-tay.note: Chinatown's big wholesale market in a 1930s building; very local, less touristy. Combine with #6.

attr-dia-dao-cu-chi-ben-dinh.name: Củ Chi Tunnels (Bến Đình)

notes.drink-bia-hoi-quan-7-kien-beo: Big Hanoi-style bia hơi beer restaurant with room for around 400 guests – fresh, cold Hanoi draught beer and a long menu of northern drinking snacks. Busy with after-work groups, families and birthday parties; football is shown on big screens. The closest proper beer restaurant to the homestay.
notes.drink-quan-an-khanh-q7-bia-hoi-ha-noi: Small, very well-rated neighbourhood bia hơi with Hanoi home cooking – reviewers single out the crispy fried rice and the fish dishes, and the fragrant, cold draught beer. Walking distance from the homestay. Street 11N (Cư xá Ngân Hàng) is earmarked by the district as a future weekend food/walking street, but its opening has not been confirmed.
notes.drink-lo-thien-quan: Lively, very local open-air drinking restaurant ('lộ thiên' means open-air) tucked away in a residential street: outdoor seating, a wide choice of dishes, cold beer and a cheerful, noisy atmosphere; the staff even put on short birthday shows. No English menu, according to reviewers.
notes.drink-brightside-bar: Live-music bar close to the homestay with live bands, open-mic and DJ nights, a creative cocktail menu, imported beers and bar snacks.
notes.drink-quan-nhau-ba-che: Big, casual quán nhậu on the same new food lot at 40 Ngô Thị Bì: beer with shared drinking dishes until 2 am. The Google rating is mixed (3.5 ★), so think of it as a cheap, lively local beer stop rather than a food destination.
notes.drink-moc-beer-grill-garden: New beer-and-grill garden on the south-east corner of the Nguyễn Hữu Thọ × Ngô Thị Bì junction (the address uses the old street name, Đường 15). Open very late – until 4 am – and very well rated so far.
notes.drink-bia-tuoi-kho-muc: Small, simple draught-beer spot – 'bia tươi' is fresh draught beer and 'khô mực' (dried squid) is the classic beer snack. Tucked into the lane at 178/4a Nguyễn Hữu Thọ on the south-east side of the junction. Very new, with only one Google review so far.
notes.drink-than-hoa-quan: Small charcoal-grill eatery ('than hoả' means charcoal fire) at 178 Nguyễn Hữu Thọ, on the south-east side of the junction. New, with only four Google reviews so far.
notes.drink-joyjoy-garden: Open-air beer garden on the newly opened food lot at 40 Ngô Thị Bì – the north-east corner of the big Nguyễn Hữu Thọ × Ngô Thị Bì junction, opposite Sunrise City View. Opening hours are not yet, so check before you go; evenings are the time to come.
notes.drink-xom-dem-quan-7: Late-night restaurant directly on Nguyễn Hữu Thọ, just north of the junction. Its Facebook page lists seafood, roast goat (dê quay) and hotpot & grill; open from morning until 4 am.
notes.drink-quan-bia-set: Big, busy beer restaurant at the start of Nguyễn Hữu Thọ known for 'bia sệt' – beer served ice-cold until it turns slushy – plus a long list of drinking snacks. Good for groups.
notes.drink-aroma-hops-eatery-drinks: Small, cosy bar-eatery with friendly English-speaking bartenders, classic cocktails, beer and bottle service, good music and tasty, affordable drinking food. Reviews are very positive.
notes.drink-bia-hoi-ha-noi-hoan-luong: Very highly rated Hanoi bia hơi with outdoor seating: beer poured fresh from the tap, northern dishes including goat meat, cheerful noisy atmosphere – reviewers say it is perfect for big groups of 20+.
notes.drink-thuong-rooftop: Rooftop café-bar on the 7th floor with retro décor and a wide view over the city towards Landmark 81 and Bitexco – great for sunset. Cocktails, mocktails, beer and snacks at modest prices. Opens in the late afternoon and gets busy with couples and groups after dark.
notes.drink-toi-ben-food-beer: Large, no-frills quán nhậu on Bến Vân Đồn with fresh seafood and classic drinking dishes, popular with office groups and football fans late into the night.
notes.drink-quan-oc-kenh-te-2: Local snail-and-seafood (ốc) eatery on the District 4 side of the Kênh Tẻ canal, a little hard to find. Reviewers praise big, fresh snails and seafood at fair prices (the salted-egg-sauce snails are a favourite), with an English-speaking waiter; it gets crowded at weekends and dishes can take a while. Just across the canal, so it is quick to reach.
notes.drink-nha-hang-wbw-world-of-beers-wine: Beer-and-wine restaurant at the Hồ Bán Nguyệt (Crescent Lake): a large selection of local and international beers on tap and in bottles (including Belgian), live music and football on weekends.
notes.drink-oc-oanh: The most famous – and most crowded – snail restaurant on Vĩnh Khánh street, with thousands of reviews. Big menu of snails, clams, prawns, octopus and grilled chicken feet; beer by the can or bottle. Expect queues and a tourist crowd at peak times; the rating is mixed, but the atmosphere is the real Vĩnh Khánh experience.
notes.drink-mr-craft-craft-beer-wine: Craft beer and wine bar with around 20 taps, just east of the Night Town zone. Reviewers like the IPAs, tacos, oysters and chicken wings, sports on TV and live bands on Saturday nights.
notes.drink-the-gioi-bo-nuong-sot-va-lau: 'Beef World' at the northern end of Vĩnh Khánh: beef grilled at the table, beef in sauces and beef hotpot. Outdoor tables are cooler and less smoky; little English is spoken. Beer is Tiger or Heineken.
notes.drink-bia-hoi-ha-noi-80a-bia-hoi-80a-qua: Authentic Hanoi bia hơi on the Bến Vân Đồn riverside road: little plastic chairs, light fresh draught beer by the jug, garlic snails, tamarind clams and peanuts, full of locals and few tourists. Tip from a reviewer: there is a second bia hơi next door – 80A is the one with the blue chairs, not the corner one.
notes.drink-oc-dao-2: One of the best-known snail restaurants on Vĩnh Khánh food street. Has an English menu that lists the cooking styles (grilled, garlic butter, tamarind, etc.), which makes ordering easy. Cheap beer, eaten street-side among locals.
notes.drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-phu-my-h: Pasteur Street's taproom and restaurant in the Crescent Residence complex near Crescent Mall and the Hồ Bán Nguyệt lake – craft beer on tap with a full menu; easy to combine with an evening walk around the lake.
notes.drink-lang-restaurant-lang-quan: Busy, inexpensive quán nhậu on Vĩnh Khánh street serving seafood and grilled dishes – a favourite with young locals for long evenings, open until 4 am. Reviewers mention good value, people-watching and occasional live music.
notes.drink-el-baron-saigon-whiskey-cigar-loun: Refined whiskey and cigar lounge for quiet conversations, date nights and small celebrations, with reserved seating and attentive service. The upmarket option in the Night Town zone.
notes.drink-ruby-soho: Rock 'n' roll pub inside the Night Town zone, decorated with music and film memorabilia, with a street-side patio for watching the evening bustle. Good cocktails, fairly priced beer, private rooms upstairs and a mix of locals and expats; live music nights.
notes.drink-tiem-bia-ga-rooster-beers-taproom-: Casual, retro-style taproom of the local Rooster Beers brewery – affordable craft beer, a laid-back crowd and only a few simple snacks. The farthest bar on this map.
notes.drink-pasteur-street-craft-beer-nguyen-d: NEW: Vietnam's pioneering craft brewery opened this taproom (its 14th) on 5 September 2025. Rotating Pasteur Street craft beers on tap plus a full food menu.
notes.drink-moon-1984-rooftop: Korean-style rooftop bar in the heart of the Night Town zone: cocktails, beer and soju happy hours, Korean food (the kimchi pancake gets praise) and fun party games. Good for dates and groups.
notes.drink-the-tavern-pmh: Long-running sports bar and pub (around 20 years) with Western and Mexican pub food, live sports on big screens (Premier League, F1, UFC, AFL), a free pool table, regular live music and quiz nights. Happy hour Mon–Fri 16:00–19:00. On the eastern edge of the Night Town zone.
notes.drink-saigon-craft-bar-tay-ta: Relaxed craft-beer pub in Phú Mỹ Hưng with 27 beers on tap and a mixed Asian/Western food menu; describes itself as a pioneer of craft beer in District 7.

notes.shop-cho-tan-kieng-1: The closest market to the homestay – a small, everyday neighbourhood market on Trần Xuân Soạn, about 550 m west of the homestay. Perfect for a first look at a Vietnamese wet market and a cheap breakfast.
notes.shop-circle-k-lam-van-ben: Open around the clock: drinks, snacks, ready meals.
notes.shop-gs25: Korean convenience store with snacks and hot food.
notes.shop-cho-cu-xa-ngan-hang: Small neighbourhood market for daily needs in the Cư xá Ngân Hàng residential area.
notes.shop-bach-hoa-xanh: Bách Hóa Xanh branch on the same street as the house (to the west). According to reviews, meat is discounted from 6–7 pm, but then it gets busy.
notes.shop-cho-tan-quy: Locals call it the 'morning market'. The covered hall itself is quiet these days – the real market happens outside: a long line of vendors' carts and pavement stalls fills Đường số 17 and the side streets around the hall. One of the liveliest street markets near the homestay.
notes.shop-cho-tan-kieng-2: A genuinely hidden market: the small hall sits inside the block behind Lê Văn Lương, and reviewers say it is hard to find the way in if you are not local. Motorbikes can ride right in between the stalls.
notes.shop-bach-hoa-xanh-122-lam-van-ben: Branch of the big Vietnamese grocery chain: fruit, vegetables, meat, fish, drinks, household goods – low fixed prices. Fresh food often discounted in the evening.
notes.shop-satra-foods: Small grocery supermarket (state-owned Satra chain), fresh meat & vegetables.
notes.shop-lotte-mart-nam-sai-gon: Cinema in the LOTTE Mart building (same building as kidzooona).
notes.shop-cho-tan-my: Big, busy and well-stocked – the best 'real' market experience in Phú Mỹ Hưng's neighbourhood.
notes.shop-go-nguyen-thi-thap: Large hypermarket (Central Retail) with a small shopping centre: groceries, household, electronics – good prices.

notes.shop-co-op-food: Small Saigon Co.op grocery store for quick shopping.
notes.shop-aeon-nguyen-van-linh: Japanese supermarket: fresh food, ready meals and high-quality household goods.

notes.shop-satra-foods-107-nguyen-tat-thanh: Small grocery supermarket in old District 4.
notes.shop-cho-xom-chieu: District 4's only official traditional market, built in 1985. Shop for fresh food in the morning; in the late afternoon and evening the streets around the hall turn into a food paradise – snails (ốc), phá lấu, crab soup and chè.
notes.shop-co-opxtra-tan-phong: Large Vietnamese hypermarket (Saigon Co.op), good-value everyday items.

practical.sub: Arrival, transport, money, safety, phrases and emergency contacts for guests of ASCON LIVING
practical.intro: Facts checked on 9 Oct 2026. Prices, fares, opening hours and rules change often in Vietnam, so ranges are given with their source and date. Always double-check anything critical (visa, health, money) with the official source.

admin_reform.text: On 1 July 2025 Vietnam abolished the district level (Quận / Huyện) and merged wards (Resolution 203/2025/QH15 and Resolution 1685/NQ-UBTVQH15 of 16 Jun 2025). Hồ Chí Minh City also merged with Bình Dương and Bà Rịa–Vũng Tàu and now has 168 units (113 wards, 54 communes, 1 special zone). Addresses are now written as house number + street + Phường (ward) + city, without a district. Our homestay was in Phường Tân Phong, Quận 7; it is now Phường Tân Hưng (merged from the former Tân Phong, Tân Quy, Tân Kiểng and Tân Hưng wards of District 7). Old names ("District 7", "Phú Mỹ Hưng", "District 1") are still widely used in conversation and on old maps and signs, so drivers understand both. Some apps may still show old addresses.

sections.h2: First time in Vietnam? The 10 essentials
sections.intro: A one-page cheat sheet. Details follow in the sections below.
items: Show this to any driver: 389A Trần Xuân Soạn, Phường Tân Hưng, Thành phố Hồ Chí Minh. The full show-to-driver card is in the section "Show-to-driver & show-to-waiter cards".

Walk at a slow, steady pace and keep going; motorbikes will flow around you. Do not run and do not step back suddenly. Use zebra crossings and traffic lights where they exist, and raise a hand to make yourself visible.
Vietnam uses only notes, no coins. Check the zeros: 10,000 vs 100,000 and 20,000 vs 500,000 (both blue) are the classic mix-ups. Prices are often written with "k": 50k = 50,000 VND.
Not expected, but appreciated. Check the bill for a 5–10% service charge first.
Take your shoes off when you enter a private home and many temple halls; look for shoes at the door.
Malls, cafés and restaurants have the cleanest toilets. Carry tissues and hand sanitiser.
Do not drink tap water; use bottled or filtered water, also for brushing teeth (US CDC advice).
Book cars and motorbike taxis in an app (Grab, Xanh SM, Be): the price is shown before you ride. Check the number plate before you get in.

It is warm all year (about 31–35 °C by day). From May to November, short tropical showers usually come in the afternoon. Caught in a tropical downpour? Just pop into the nearest café and wait it out – it usually passes within 20–30 minutes.
Some small family-run shops and offices pause around midday, but large museums and malls stay open (for example Dinh Độc Lập / Independence Palace: 07:00–18:00 daily, as of October 2026).
Police 113 · Fire 114 · Ambulance 115 (voice calls, free). For international-standard care: FV Hospital, emergency (028) 35 11 35 00. Save your host's phone number too.

sections.h2: Arriving at Tân Sơn Nhất Airport (SGN)
sections.intro: Tân Sơn Nhất is about 13–14 km by road from the homestay. It has three terminals; check your ticket for the terminal.
items: As of October 2026: T2: international flights. T1: domestic flights of VietJet Air. T3: domestic flights of Vietnam Airlines, Pacific Airlines, VASCO, Bamboo Airways, Vietravel Airlines and Sun PhuQuoc Airways (Southern Airports Corporation / Vietnam Airlines). Airlines can move terminals; check your booking.

Road distance to the homestay: T2 13.03 km, T1 12.74 km, T3 14.06 km. Estimated car time in normal traffic: about 29–30 minutes. In rush hours (roughly 07:00–09:00 and 16:30–19:00), in heavy rain or in the days before Tết, allow 45–60+ minutes.

Book a car in the Grab app after you have your luggage. Grab's official HCMC car fare (grab.com, as of October 2026): GrabCar 4-seat from 25,000 VND for the first 2 km, then 9,000 VND/km plus 300 VND/min; 7-seat from 30,000 VND, then 11,000 VND/km. On that basis a trip to the homestay works out at roughly 133,000–152,000 VND for a 4-seater in normal conditions. Surge pricing (rush hour, rain), a night surcharge (10,000 VND, 22:00–05:59), tolls and airport fees are added on top, so the app may show more; third-party guides quote up to 250,000–300,000 VND. The app always shows the final price before you book. Estimate as of October 2026; varies with time of day and demand.
As of October 2026: T3: ground floor, PNA car park. T1: lane D1. T2: follow the "Ride-hailing / Grab" signs to the car park. Grab charges no airport surcharge for pickups at T3.

Xanh SM (international brand Green SM) runs electric taxis and app cars at all terminals. As of October 2026: T3: lane A, pillars 11A–15A; T1: taxi at pillars C3–C6, app cars lane D2; T2: lane A, pillars A1–A4. Metered fares in HCMC start at around 27,500–34,400 VND for the first 2 km (unofficial fare table). Estimate as of October 2026; varies with time of day and demand.

If you take a regular taxi, use the official queue and well-known companies (Vinasun, Mai Linh); make sure the meter is running. Avoid touts in the arrival hall and fixed-price offers well above the app price.

Bus 109 runs between T3 and the Saigon Bus Station (Bến xe buýt Sài Gòn, Công viên 23/9, District 1 area), roughly from early morning until late evening; fare about 15,000–20,000 VND. Bus 152 runs T1/T2 – Bến Thành – Trung Sơn during the day; fare 5,000 VND. Estimate as of October 2026; varies with time of day and demand. No bus goes directly to the homestay: take the bus to the centre and a Grab from there. With luggage, a direct Grab or taxi is much easier.
Get a SIM/eSIM (see "SIM cards & eSIM"), withdraw a small amount of cash at a bank ATM, and send your host your flight number and estimated arrival time.

sections.intro: Ride-hailing apps are the easiest way to move around Hồ Chí Minh City. Walking is fine for short distances in the neighbourhood.
items: The most widely used app: GrabCar (4 or 7 seats) and GrabBike (motorbike taxi). Price shown upfront; pay by card in the app or cash. English interface. Check the number plate, driver name and photo before you get in.

Electric cars and motorbikes (VinFast) from the company GSM. English app; you can also wave down its green taxis. International cards (Visa, Mastercard, JCB) are accepted in the app, but some foreign cards fail; cash is the fallback. A Vietnamese phone number makes sign-up easier.
Vietnamese app with motorbikes (beBike) and cars (beCar). Sign-up works best with a Vietnamese (+84) phone number; foreign-card support is not guaranteed, so plan to pay cash.
Gojek left Vietnam on 16 Sep 2024; the app no longer works here.

Traditional motorbike drivers wait at corners. Agree on the price before you get on, insist on a helmet and keep your bag in front of you. An app motorbike (GrabBike, Xanh SM Bike, beBike) is usually cheaper and safer because the fare is fixed.

Cheap (a few thousand đồng per ride, e.g. 5,000 VND on route 152; airport bus 109 costs more) but slower, with few English signs. Use Google Maps for routes; routes change from time to time, so check the app or the stop before you ride. Estimate as of October 2026; varies with time of day and demand.

HCMC's first metro line runs Bến Thành – Suối Tiên (towards Thủ Đức), opened 22 Dec 2024. As of October 2026: fares 7,000–20,000 VND cash (6,000–19,000 VND cashless); 1-day pass 40,000 VND, 3-day pass 90,000 VND; contactless Visa, Mastercard, JCB, Amex and UnionPay cards are accepted at the gates. Trains run from early morning until late evening; check current hours at the station. The metro does not reach Tân Hưng; take a Grab to Bến Thành first.
Footpaths are often used for parking motorbikes or as shop space, so you may need to walk at the edge of the road. Watch for motorbikes riding against the flow, and see "Crossing the street" above.

Drivers rarely read English addresses. Show the Vietnamese address with diacritics (accent marks) from this guide or from Google Maps. Since 1 Jul 2025 addresses no longer include a district (Quận); see the box "New ward names".

sections.h2: Common scams & how to avoid them
sections.intro: Most visitors have no trouble. These are the tricks reported in the Vietnamese press; knowing them is usually enough.
items: Someone starts cleaning or "repairing" your shoes without asking, then demands a very high price. Say Không, cảm ơn (no, thank you) firmly and walk on. Tuổi Trẻ reported an organised group in central HCMC in 2026 that also pickpocketed tourists.

A seller puts a coconut, fruit basket or hat in your hands for a photo, then asks for a big sum. Ask the price first and don't accept items you didn't ask for. Vietnamese media reported a case of 330,000 VND for one coconut (2025–2026).

Rigged or "fast" meters, long detours, or a driver who says you paid with 10,000 instead of 100,000 VND. Use app rides with upfront prices, or Vinasun / Mai Linh taxis; pay with the exact amount and count the notes aloud. Vietnamese newspapers reported a taxi driver swapping a 200,000 note for 10,000 in Jan 2026.

Someone approaches you saying "Grab?". Only get into the car that the app assigned: check the plate number, car model, driver name and photo. If they don't match, don't get in and report it in the app.
Avoid people offering rides inside the arrival hall. Use the Grab/Xanh SM pickup points or the official taxi queue.

Change money only at banks, licensed exchange counters or authorised gold shops/agents. Exchanging at unlicensed places is illegal; the buyer can also be fined (Decree 340/2025/NĐ-CP, effective 9 Feb 2026).
Many look-alike sites charge extra for "express" e-visas. The official portal is evisa.gov.vn.

Thieves on motorbikes sometimes grab phones and bags. Keep your phone away from the kerb side, wear bags across the body, and don't hold your phone out while standing on the roadside or riding pillion.
Report to the police (113) or the HCMC tourism hotline (028) 1022, then press 8 (HCMC Department of Tourism, 2025), and tell your host.

sections.intro: A local SIM gives you a Vietnamese number (+84), which helps with ride-hailing apps and deliveries.
items: Official mobile-operator counters (e.g. Viettel) are in the T2 arrival hall after customs. Buy only from official counters or shops; unofficial sellers may sell SIMs that are later blocked. You must show your physical passport.

From the official Viettel page, SIM card price extra: 5G60T 60,000 VND – 5 GB/day, 7 days; 5G80T 80,000 VND – 5 GB/day, 15 days; 5G150T 150,000 VND – 5 GB/day, 30 days; 5G180H 180,000 VND – 5 GB/day plus calls, 30 days. Airport counters often sell bundles at about 290,000–300,000 VND for 30 days (traveller reports). Compare with the official prices. Estimate as of October 2026; plans and prices change.

As of October 2026, foreigners' passport-registered SIMs must be verified with a facial biometric check (Circular 08/2026/TT-BKHCN, in force since 15 Apr 2026). If the SIM is later moved to another phone, outgoing service can be suspended until you verify again. Tip: do the registration in the phone you will actually use.

A data-only travel eSIM from an international provider needs no Vietnamese registration, but gives no +84 number (fine for maps, Grab and messaging). Check that your phone supports eSIM and is not network-locked.
Most cafés, restaurants and malls offer free Wi-Fi; ask for the password: Mật khẩu wifi là gì?

sections.intro: The currency is the Vietnamese đồng (VND). Exchange rates move; as of October 2026 one US dollar is roughly 26,000 VND. Check a live rate before you exchange.
items: Notes only (coins are no longer used). Common notes: 10,000 (tan-brown), 20,000 (blue), 50,000 (pink-red), 100,000 (green), 200,000 (red-brown), 500,000 (cyan-blue). Notes from 10,000 up are polymer (plastic). Small notes (1,000, 2,000, 5,000) are paper.

20,000 vs 500,000: both are blue; the 500,000 is longer (152 mm vs 136 mm) and a lighter cyan-blue. 10,000 vs 100,000: different colours (tan vs green) but the same number of digits at a glance – count the zeros. Keep large and small notes in separate pockets.

Use ATMs inside or next to a bank branch. Nearest: Techcombank ATM (Trần Xuân Soạn / Lâm Văn Bền) – 0.6 km, about 8 min walk; Agribank ATM (Đường số 17) – 0.9 km, about 12 min; Techcombank ATM (Lâm Văn Bền) – 1.0 km, about 14 min, listed as 24/7; VietinBank ATM (Ngô Thị Nhạn) – 1.3 km, about 17 min; Agribank ATM (Lê Văn Lương) – 1.4 km, about 19 min; BIDV ATM (Nguyễn Thị Thập, near LOTTE Mart) – 2.0 km, about 26 min, listed as 24/7. Locations are approximate.

Many ATMs limit each withdrawal to about 2–3 million VND; foreign cards are usually charged a fee per withdrawal (traveller reports: about 50,000–55,000 VND or a percentage, depending on the bank; estimate as of October 2026). If the ATM or card terminal offers to charge you in your home currency, decline (choose VND); the conversion is usually worse.

Use banks, licensed exchange counters, or authorised gold shops/agents that display a licence. Unlicensed exchange is illegal and the customer can be fined under Decree 340/2025/NĐ-CP (from 9 Feb 2026): a warning for amounts under USD 1,000, fines of 10–20 million VND above that, plus confiscation. Bring clean, undamaged notes; torn or old USD notes may be refused.

Visa and Mastercard work in hotels, malls, supermarkets, chains and many mid-range restaurants. Street food, markets and small shops want cash. Vietnamese QR payments (VietQR) need a local bank account, but visitors with some apps from China (WeChat Pay, Alipay), Singapore, South Korea, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia can pay at VietQR codes via cross-border links (as of October 2026).

Not expected and never compulsory. First check the bill for a service charge (5–10% in some restaurants and hotels). If you want to tip: leave small change or round up in restaurants; porters 20,000–50,000 VND per bag; private guides about 100,000–200,000 VND per day; private drivers 50,000–100,000 VND per day (Vietnam tourism guidance, as of October 2026). Tipping app drivers in the app or in cash is optional.

Expected at markets, souvenir stalls and with street vendors: ask the price, offer less, stay friendly and walk away if it's too high. Not done in supermarkets, malls, chain stores, restaurants with menus, or for app rides.

sections.intro: Save these numbers before you need them. Calls to 112–115 are free from any phone.
items: 113 Police · 114 Fire & rescue · 115 Ambulance · 112 National search & rescue / incident line (Ministry of Science and Technology; Government decision, effective 15 Sep 2025). Operators may speak little English – ask a local or your host to help, or say your location slowly and show the address card.

113, 114 and 115 are voice calls only; there is no public SMS emergency service. Agree with your host in advance that you can text or message the host as a backup, and keep the card "Vui lòng viết ra giúp tôi" (please write it down) ready. FV Hospital lists sign-language support.
Recommended for international guests: FV Hospital

Bệnh viện FV, 6 Nguyễn Lương Bằng, Phường Tân Mỹ. 24/7 emergency department including children's emergencies; emergency & ambulance (028) 35 11 35 00; general information (028) 35 11 33 33. Free 24/7 interpreters (English, French, Japanese, Korean, Chinese, Russian, Khmer). 3.13 km by road · car about 10 min · motorbike about 8 min · walk 3.15 km, about 42 min.

Bệnh viện Đa khoa Tân Hưng (Tân Hưng General Hospital), 871 Trần Xuân Soạn, Phường Tân Hưng; emergency 0901 34 69 34, switchboard (028) 377 606 48. 1.67 km by road · car about 5 min · motorbike about 4 min · walk 1.67 km, about 22 min (map position approximate). English-speaking staff not confirmed.
Phòng khám Đa khoa Tâm Anh Quận 7 (Tâm Anh General Clinic, an outpatient clinic with an emergency area for adults and children), Sunrise City, 25 Nguyễn Hữu Thọ, Phường Tân Hưng; 0287 102 6789 / 093 180 6858. 2.09 km by road · car about 7 min · motorbike about 5 min · walk 2.11 km, about 28 min. Serious cases are transferred to a hospital.

Bệnh viện Đa khoa Nguyễn Thị Thập (formerly District 7 Hospital), 101 Nguyễn Thị Thập, Phường Tân Mỹ; emergency 028 3773 1421. 3.11 km by road · car about 10 min · motorbike about 7 min · walk 3.17 km, about 42 min.
Bệnh viện Đa khoa Khánh Hội (formerly District 4 Hospital), 63–65 Bến Vân Đồn, Phường Xóm Chiếu; 028 3826 1568. 4.34 km by road · car about 11 min · motorbike about 8 min · walk 2.87 km, about 38 min. English at public hospitals is limited; bring a Vietnamese speaker if you can.

For a child emergency, FV Hospital (above) is the closest with 24/7 paediatric emergency care and interpreters. The city's large public children's hospital is Bệnh viện Nhi Đồng Thành phố, 15 Võ Trần Chí, Xã Tân Nhựt (24/7 emergency department); hotline 1900 1217 (bookings and advice – in an emergency call 115); switchboard 028 2253 6688. It is far away: 21.18 km by road · car about 41 min · motorbike about 32 min in normal traffic.

Pharmacity, 45 Lâm Văn Bền (open 24/7 per Pharmacity's store list): 0.93 km by road · car about 4 min · motorbike about 3 min · walk 0.94 km, about 13 min.
Pharmacity, 340 Lê Văn Lương, Phường Tân Hưng (24/7): 1.85 km by road · car about 7 min · motorbike about 5 min · walk 1.85 km, about 25 min.
Many other pharmacies (nhà thuốc), e.g. Long Châu at 621–623 Trần Xuân Soạn (06:00–23:00), are closer but not open all night.

Công an phường Tân Hưng (Tân Hưng Ward Police), 1 Đặng Đại Độ, Phường Tân Hưng. 4.28 km by road · car about 11 min · motorbike about 8 min · walk 4.32 km, about 58 min. In an emergency call 113. To report a lost passport or theft for insurance, go to the ward police with your host or a Vietnamese speaker, then contact your embassy/consulate.

As of October 2026, HCMC has no dedicated tourist police. In central tourist areas you may see "Trật tự viên du lịch" (tourism order officers, from the city's youth volunteer force working with the Department of Tourism and police) who help visitors (Thanh Niên; government portal). Tourism complaints: (028) 1022, then press 8.

Check before you travel that your insurance covers medical treatment and evacuation in Vietnam, including motorbike rides (policies often exclude riding without a licence or helmet). Hospitals may ask for a deposit or a guarantee from your insurer.

Contact your consulate if your passport is lost or stolen, or if you are arrested or seriously ill. Addresses and phone numbers below come from the consulates' own websites or the official list of the HCMC Department of Foreign Affairs (Sở Ngoại vụ TP.HCM), as of October 2026. Honorary consulates offer limited services and often need an appointment; call or email before visiting. Vietnamese citizens do not need a consulate; overseas Vietnamese travelling on a foreign passport should contact that country's consulate. Full official list of all consulates in HCMC: https://mofahcm.gov.vn/co-quan-dai-dien/lanh-su-doan-tai-thanh-pho-ho-chi-minh

sections.intro: Hồ Chí Minh City is generally safe and welcoming for visitors. A few simple habits keep your stay smooth: take care in traffic, stay cool and use mosquito repellent.
items: Don't drink tap water or use it to brush your teeth. Eat food that is cooked and served hot, and drink sealed bottles (US CDC, 2026).

Dengue is present in Vietnam all year, more so in the rainy season (US CDC; HCMC Center for Disease Control). Use mosquito repellent day and evening, wear long sleeves at dusk, and see a doctor if you get a high fever.
Daytime temperatures are 31–35 °C all year with high humidity. Drink plenty of water, plan walks for early morning or late afternoon, and use sunscreen.

Traffic is the biggest risk. On a motorbike always wear a helmet (required by law) and keep legs away from the hot exhaust pipe. Riding a motorbike yourself requires a valid Vietnamese or recognised licence and is usually not covered by insurance otherwise.

From May to November, short tropical showers usually come in the afternoon – perfect timing for a café, a museum or our rainy-day tips. Caught in a tropical downpour? Just pop into the nearest café and wait it out – it usually passes within 20–30 minutes. A light poncho or umbrella is handy.
Use the safe or lock your valuables, carry a copy/photo of your passport, and take only the cash you need for the day.

HCMC is generally considered safe for women, but harassment can occur, including from unlicensed drivers (UK FCDO travel advice, updated Sep 2026). Use app rides and share the trip from the app with a friend; sit in the back seat; don't accept drinks or food from strangers; keep your host's number saved; watch out for bag snatching from motorbikes at night.

Same-sex relationships are legal and there are no criminal penalties (UK FCDO). As of October 2026, Vietnam does not legally recognise same-sex marriage: the Law on Marriage and Family 2014 (Art. 8.2) states that the State does not recognise marriage between people of the same sex; it no longer prohibits same-sex weddings or living together. The UK FCDO describes Vietnam as generally tolerant.

Check whether you need a visa before you travel. E-visas are issued for all nationalities through the official portal evisa.gov.vn (Vietnam Immigration Department). Beware of look-alike agency sites. This guide gives no legal advice.

tet.text: Tết (Lunar New Year) falls in late January or February. Around Tết many family shops, street-food stalls and markets close for several days; supermarkets, malls, chains and larger hotels mostly stay open, sometimes with shorter hours. Transport fills up in the week before Tết, so book early. The city is festive, decorated and pleasant to walk around. Exact dates for the coming Tết are shown in the app's current notices.

sections.intro: Vietnamese people are warm and forgiving with visitors. A few gestures show respect.
items: A smile and a slight nod is enough; Xin chào (hello). Use both hands to give or receive things (money, business cards) from older people.
Never leave chopsticks standing upright in a bowl of rice (it recalls incense at funerals), and don't point with them. Place them on the rest or across the bowl.
Wait for the oldest person to start eating. Dishes are shared; take a little at a time onto your own bowl.
Take off your shoes when entering a home (including ours, if requested) and many temple and pagoda halls.
Cover shoulders and knees, speak quietly, don't point your feet at altars or Buddha statues, and ask before photographing monks or worshippers.
Ask first (point at the camera and smile). Don't photograph military or police sites.
Don't touch people – especially children – on the head; don't point with your feet.
Raising your voice or getting visibly angry rarely helps and causes loss of face; stay calm and smile, even in a dispute.

Don't assume museums close for lunch – many stay open all day. Example: Dinh Độc Lập (Independence Palace) is open daily 07:00–18:00, including weekends and holidays; adult ticket 80,000 VND (official site, as of October 2026). Check each museum's hours.
